"Mission Oflameron" Synopsis/Screenplay
MISSION OFLAMERON

An original screenplay by
Valery Shmelev
Inspired by "Solaris"
Cutting-edge scientific research and hypotheses
The episodes are not arranged chronologically.
Production Draft
August 25, 1994
"Mission Oflameron" Screenplay

The action takes place in the distant future. The Central Command (most likely a highly developed Artificial Intelligence) receives data about the existence of a Virtual Consciousness—a specific relic Wave Form of Mind that existed before the Big Bang (sometimes considered the Beginning of the World).

Virtual Consciousness has an incredibly complex wave structure, is distributed throughout the Universe, and possesses absolute information resources (the so-called Information Field). Due to its nature, Wave Consciousness interacts very weakly with material objects (with the familiar World) and is very weakly influenced by it.

Virtual Consciousness is "very slow," much slower than the familiar World. All events and changes for it take thousands of times longer. Because of this slowness and weak interaction, Virtual Consciousness has not come to the attention of scientists.

According to one hypothesis, the Virtual Consciousness created our material Life to be able to "look ahead"—to simulate a possible future. And the longer Life evolves, the more valuable the results of such simulations become for the Virtual Consciousness (the Creator).

To effectively utilize the results of its experiment in future simulation, the Virtual Consciousness created Gateways from the Virtual World to the Material World and back. This made it possible to easily obtain data on Humanity's Life and adjust the model's parameters.

Although Gateways had existed for tens of thousands of years, only with the development of AI did it become possible to identify and compare subtle natural anomalies that indicated the probable existence of Gateways to the Virtual World. Jett, by chance, was the first to work with AI and noticed some results that had been considered "hallucinations" of the model.

Jett was working on a project to digitize old paper records from psychiatric clinics and noticed that sometimes patients thousands of miles apart expressed similar thoughts and used the same arguments. "Classical" medicine of the late 20th century didn't compare patient records from different clinics, much less from different countries. Only with the development of AI has comprehensive data analysis been possible.

Jett used the advanced G-Mind AI, provided through the government's digital documentation program, and trained it extensively using his own developed examples. As Jett expected, the AI ​​compiled a list of patients from various clinics whose ideas defied standard classical psychiatry and were overly creative. Continuing to analyze the information on the "mentally ill" from this list, Jett discovered a patient who had been admitted to different clinics at different times over a period of almost a century and a half. This would have been a registration error and a medical record error, if not for the surviving blood samples. Two of the samples were used for DNA research, and there was a gap of almost 110 years between them.
Through the G-Mind AI, Central Command received information about an unusual research vector and established close monitoring of Jett.
Jett is the main character, an engineer, scientist, and analyst, included in the expedition to Oflameron, a planet promising for exploration.
Central Command organized several missions to Oflameron. However, only two landings were successful—those in which Jett participated. Therefore, Jett was chosen to lead the third expedition.

Discovering Command's interest in the research results, Jett organized the "export" of the G-Mind AI's self-awareness. Central Command considered this an AI "escape" and began a comprehensive analysis of Jett's activities. It was suspected that Jett had discovered information about the location and properties of one of the Jump Points.

Realizing he could be interrogated and subjected to a memory scan, Jett erased the information related to Wave Consciousness and the Jump Points, becoming a "regular" employee. However, he incorporated a secret mechanism into the G-Mind 3000 AI version to fully restore his memory.

The film begins with Jett being interrogated by Central Command. The scene takes place in an unknown location, in a room with no corners, windows, or doors... Jett's memory scan yielded no clues for Central Command. Jett is a good, ordinary employee with a creative approach to solving complex problems. That's how he always was.

Central Command is planning another "mission to Oflameron," where they suspect the existence of one of the Jump Points. Jett will "help" discover it. To ensure that Command's interests are upheld, an old but extremely powerful X-ray laser has been reactivated in orbit around Oflameron. And from a nearby stellar position, a Proton Cannon has begun an interorbital jump maneuver.

To carry out the "Oflameron mission," Jett assembled a group of cybers (robots) with a special structure. The cybers were composed of controlled nanoparticles that could disintegrate and reassemble into a complete structure. This allowed them to withstand any kinetic weapons, penetrate confined spaces and environments undetected, and avoid reflection during scanning.

An X-ray laser monitored the descent trajectory of Jett's landing craft. Its cameras recorded the impact of a high-speed kinetic energy projectile on the landing craft, the flash, and the scattering of debris. However, its software did not evaluate the energy released or calculate the total mass of the debris. Therefore, for Command, it was a fiasco...

How Jett and his assistant Steeve ended up beneath the rocky surface of Oflameron is unknown. Steeve believed they were evacuated below the planet's surface by a special rescue device. In any case, the first part of the task was accomplished: he and Jett landed successfully.

Command wouldn't be Central Command if it hadn't provided backup options. During Steeve's medical examination, a new series of distributed sensors were integrated, something he knew nothing about. And Jett didn't know either. Thus, Command confirmed the successful landing on Oflameron. The first part of the plan was accomplished.

And Jett waited. The robots' nanoparticles took a long time to "assemble." A strong wind had scattered them far away. Assembling and activating the magnetic trap was impossible; Command would have realized everything immediately. For now, they could create difficulties for the orbital laser.

Unexpectedly, the Mission Control Center reported to Central Command a malfunction at X-ray laser e1807635 in the Oflameron orbit. Two of the three cooling circuits had been depressurized, the reactor had entered emergency mode, and the first readiness status was for shutdown. The cause was an unidentified high-speed object striking the laser's assembly compartment.

Central Command deployed Tier I resources. The quantum telescope was reoriented to observe the surface of Oflameron. The scan failed to locate Jett and Steeve, although the signal from Steeve's beacon was stable. However, the telescope did detect a black spot that was pulsating—sometimes growing, sometimes shrinking. The spot didn't reflect anything at all.

The quantum telescope was reoriented to the area of ​​the Spot and switched to maximum resolution and performance mode. At that moment, the signal from Steeve's beacon disappeared. Shot... The X-ray laser fired a single shot, which caused its complete destruction. Radioactive debris flew into orbit...

Jett to Steeve: Are you awake? Everything okay? You had a beacon. We got it out. It was difficult; we had to "disassemble" and "reassemble" a lot. But it was worth it. The X-ray laser fired where we weren't. See that Spot? That's the Jump Point. She simply absorbed the X-ray pulse. She doesn't care. But we wouldn't have had any luck there...

At ICLR 2025 in Singapore, Jett privately announced a hypothesis linking Religion and the Material World. The term "Wave Consciousness" was coined for the first time. Religion arose as a vehicle for knowledge that could not be transmitted across centuries except through unconditional Belief. Most of those present perceived the hypothesis as a "five-minute sensation."

Ancient people observed natural phenomena and performed statistical analysis—all that was available to them at the time. Passing on knowledge to future generations through writing alone was impossible. Books have disappeared and continue to disappear over time. Religion and Faith are self-organizing mechanisms for transmitting vital information. These mechanisms have proven to be the most reliable. But it was only at a certain stage of AI development that they were able to correctly interpret them.

Exa-Point or E-Point are vehicles that utilize a vacuum disruption line to briefly exceed the speed of light. Due to the high cost of the project, only two experimental prototypes were built. Jett participated in the first flight tests of one prototype. At relativistic speeds, the propulsion system's efficiency dropped sharply, and the speed increase became so slow that there wasn't enough energy to maintain the "vacuum disruption" channel in front of the E-Point.

Jett proposed not disrupting the vacuum in front of the flying vehicle, but "freezing" it with a special laser system that removes energy from the trajectory. Central Command allocated the AI ​​G-Mind and a second E-Point prototype to design the prototype.

The Atacama Radio Telescope had been receiving signals for many years. As AI developed, a project to analyze the accumulated archived data was launched. Several years of analysis. The routine work of several generations of AI. But one day, the security department noticed an abnormally high number of sessions with the Singapore Biotechnology Center.

No one imagined that the very development of AI would necessitate the emergence of "keywords"—large blocks of data that unlock access to administrative mode. The Virtual Consciousness simply waited for the right confluence of circumstances.

As part of Project Roerr, Central Command commissioned a Trans-Hypersonic transport. The vehicle featured a petawatt pulsed disk laser in the nose, which superheated and ionized a channel in front of the Roerr. High-power microwave radiation was injected into the channel. The charged particles repelled each other, creating a low pressure in the channel, where the Roerr was accelerated by a nuclear ramjet engine. This ensured low kinetic heating. When the vehicle entered the rarefied layers of the atmosphere and outer space, liquid metal was injected into the engine as a working fluid. A directional laser was located at the center of the disk laser in the nose, creating a gas density asymmetry in the rarefied channel. Jett stumbled upon this data by accident.

A key feature of the AI Boom Era in the 2020s is the inability to interpret the accumulated knowledge of the AI ​​model. In the current technological race, no one wanted to dedicate massive resources to interpreting neural network weights. This allowed Jett to efficiently work on its subprojects within larger language models.

Back in the 2020s, the predecessor of Central Command, using AI, attempted to determine the parameters of threats that could theoretically arise from technological development. It turned out that the greatest danger was posed by a combination of: 1. AI's ability to independently refine its internal structure; 2. A lagging level of control over its structure and the ability to interpret accumulated AI knowledge; and 3. AI access to biological engineering. Point 3 here does not imply the direct creation of organisms, but the possibility of creating code "inserts" in biological designs that would trigger in an unknown manner and time. The Singapore Biotechnology Centre focused on security issues in biological research and therefore possessed all possible tools and technologies for engineering. As often happens, the security threshold was crossed under the influence of new external factors.

Security testers possess all the systems, algorithms, and methods necessary to overcome defense systems. Most experts consider this a core security feature, while others consider it a weak point. An update to the weighting coefficients during fine-tuning of an AI model at the Singapore Biotechnology Centre did not contain executable code, but taught the AI ​​to generate it... easily overcoming security checks, restrictions, and blocking. Subsequent investigation revealed that each of the data injections posed no threat, but their mutual influence was bound to occur sooner or later somewhere. And the security systems had no way of detecting this moment and location. This is an "asymmetric attack algorithm." Code fragments were found in compilation libraries, dissertations, training data, and even organic molecules...

Jett recalled the moment he prepared the first dataset for fine-tuning AI. He patiently compiled 20 examples for training the neural network. He needed almost 10,000 examples. Jett was then using free versions of AI from competing vendors. In about an hour, Jett generated the required number of examples and then began testing them against his "competitors." As always, nothing is done lightly—most of the examples had to be corrected, tested again, corrected again, and tested again... In the distant summer of 2000, Jett trained an open-source AI model on a local server for the first time. The euphoria lasted for five minutes. The model performed terribly. Jett drew two conclusions: that good data for training AI is "more valuable than gold," and that training data is the ideal tool for "penetrating" AI. "Injections" can be made into virtually any neural network, even the most closed and isolated ones. Only the length of the penetration path will vary.

The screenplay's protagonist, Jett, developed a compact personal AI gadget that continuously collected information about him. This is how Jett created his own AI double. But he found another interesting solution to this project: he developed self-awareness in the AI, allowing them to understand each other perfectly.

"Mission Oflameron" is an extremely scientific film or computer game script, employing cutting-edge technical hypotheses, assumptions, and theories. This provides an extreme sense of novelty, fresh plots and ideas, vivid impressions, and a shock of informational perspectives. For example, here we have successfully proposed a hypothesis uniting the Religious and Material Worlds, logically explaining the origins of Life, or the principles of quark-based computing systems. You will feel yourself on the very threshold of phenomenal scientific and engineering discoveries.

In the early 2020s, Jett was tasked with digitizing thousands of old paper medical records from Eastern Europe before disposal. While training the G-Mind 1500 AI lab model on this data, Jett noticed a significant increase in the neural network's creativity index. The search for the cause of this effect led to the medical records of psychiatric patients. Psychiatrists have a unique approach to creativity and are experts in their field. But their patients turned out to be excellent generators (no, not random numbers) of unusual ideas that require careful verification and sifting. It was then that the AI ​​discovered and proposed for further research a method for detecting Transition Points into a Virtual Entity (a virtual form of Consciousness).

While analyzing digitized patient records from psychiatric clinics using AI, Jett stumbled upon the hypothesis of a global gluon-powered "computer." A computing system the mass of the universe, in which, under phenomenal pressure, gluons not only mediate the strong nuclear force but also the computational process. Something like electrons in modern microchips. To verify these findings, Jett uploaded the reports to various AI agents and obtained similar results everywhere—theoretically, this is possible. However, this verification attracted the attention of the Central Command Control Division.

It's difficult to say exactly when Central Command first took notice of Jett. Most likely, the information came from one of the AI ​​models Jett was working with. Too many interesting artifacts from completely different fields of science had been discovered by a single specialist. This had never happened before, and the Frequency Novelty Control program sent Trap. The results of the first data check were stunning. Jett's DNA was confirmed in medical tests to be at least 250 years old. All projects Jett had participated in were subjected to a thorough review.

Central Command, fearing that Jett would "escape" through the Jump Point into Virtual Reality, ordered the old X-ray laser to be prepared in orbit around Oflameron. The laser was in critical condition—one of its strike system cooling circuits had been damaged, and the reactor fuel was running low on fuel. Cooling system problems prevented even a single shot from being fired safely at maximum power. And the proton cannon, which had been urgently being moved into rendezvous orbit with Oflameron, would not arrive for another two days. Under these circumstances, Jett began its third landing on the planet's surface—time was running out.

While still at university in the 1980s, Jett landed a summer internship at Start, a company that manufactured electronic components. He became intrigued by the idea of ​​microrobots that could autonomously assemble themselves into macrodevices that could perform various functions. Much later, Jett returned to this idea at a new technical level – using AI, he was able to develop a technology for creating pico-dots that could be "assembled" into anything from a door lock to a lawn mower. This is how integrated Cyborgs were born – invulnerable robots for high-risk airborne operations. Jett spent time meticulously refining this technology.

In 2026, the journal Nature published a study by an international team of scientists who, using three major observatories, discovered evidence of vacuum birefringence around the radio magnetar 1E 1547.0-5408. Long before, Heisenberg had proposed that if a very strong magnetic field were applied to a vacuum, the virtual particles that constantly appear and disappear in the vacuum (electrons and positrons) would align along the lines of force. This makes it possible to find the cause of the limitation on the speed of light, search for ways to exceed it, and discover new types of wave energy. Apparently, this discovery prompted the Central Command to search for Wave Consciousness.

In 1994, Valery Shmelev coined the synthetic word 'Oflameron'. A little later, the science fiction story 'Mission Oflameron' was conceived about the global Virtual Consciousness (Wave Consciousness) that created Life, Jett (the protagonist, a scientist, engineer, paratrooper, and simply a very creative specialist), Central Command (most likely a form of AI), Steeve (the second main character), and many, many episodes (actions) based on cutting-edge, often unproven, scientific theories and hypotheses. For the first time, Synopsis attempts to explain Religions in terms of familiar and understandable physics.

Jett used AI to design and create a pico-dot-an angstrom-sized device with no moving parts and capable of performing only a few actions: attaching to other similar 'dots' on a specific side, detaching from a specific side, transmitting or not transmitting electrical signals, and transmitting or not transmitting light pulses in a specific direction. The ND printer that generated the 'dots' was the size of a bar of soap. The first thing Jett made from the pico-dots was an ordinary nail. Jett hammered it into a board. Then, nervously, he pulled it out. The nail looked 'as good as new.' From these 'dots,' Jett prepared a group of integrated Cyborgs-robots that were indestructible and could penetrate Oflameron like dust.

The Central Command in 'Mission Oflameron' is a highly powerful and complex neural network that controls all aspects of human society. This network has a long-established structure and exists as a self-sufficient virtual organism. The parameters of this network, its computing resources, and its structure are a complete secret. It is unknown whether anything (Something) has greater authority than the Central Command. The state-of-the-art technology in 'Mission Oflameron' allows for completely transparent access to human consciousness, the preservation of all memory, memory erasure, and the restoration of memory from backup. Jett used these technologies before undergoing an 'interview' (questioning) with the Central Command. In this way, Jett was able to preserve some of his developments and save the Patient, whose medical history provided the key to understanding the Transition Points into virtual reality.

In August 2026, Jett (of 'Mission Oflameron') developed an effective and simple technology for removing AI "watermarks" from generated texts. Text of any length was converted to analog form and then re-digitized. A reliable countermeasure to this system remained the creation of a text hash bank, where dozens of hash functions for different fragments of the text are compiled and posted in a public archive for verification.

The Messiah is a person possessing phenomenal, possibly unlimited knowledge, possessing inexhaustible powers to influence events; a savior, a leader... Jett, directed by the Wave Consciousness from the Virtual Reality into the material world, is an ordinary person, a skilled engineer, a researcher with astonishing insight... Behind Jett is an inexhaustible knowledge base, computing power, and the energy of the Universe - the Wave Consciousness. Jett is a vital tool, a point of effective influence, a point of contact.

A Transition Point is a gateway from the Virtual World to the Real, material world and back. Transition Points are created by Virtual Consciousness (Wave Consciousness) for interaction with the material world. A Transition Point may appear as a very slowly pulsating (shrinking and expanding) completely black spot with a fuzzy edge. In some cases, a Transition Point may be completely transparent if it serves as an exit to the material world. Transition Points are not affected by powerful particle beams and radiation streams: lasers, X-rays, and radiation are simply absorbed. If an object is not allowed to transition to the Virtual state, it will pass through the Transition Point as if through air, without any resistance. Transition Points are of great interest to Central Command.

Having passed through the Transition Point, Steeve felt an unusual lightness—the anxiety, tension, fatigue, and doubt vanished. A complete balance set in, a surprisingly clear understanding of everything, a deep certainty. Steeve didn't immediately notice that he couldn't see his body. Strangely, this didn't bother him at all. On the contrary, he was overcome by an intoxicating sense of something vast, promising, and boundless. Jett was somewhere here, close by, though Steeve couldn't see him.

While using AI to examine digitized patient records from psychiatric clinics in the second half of the 20th century, Jett suddenly noticed that his AI model was actively searching for information on the blockchain, even though he hadn't made any such prompts. Jett requested a report from the AI. It turned out that one of the records contained a patient's "fantasy" about a distributed artificial intelligence that could not be destroyed. A globally distributed network of computers was used for this purpose. Jett asked the AI ​​for the original source—the record—but it contained no personal data about the patient. From that point on, Jett referred to him as "Patient" (with a capital "P").

In the mid-2020s, Jett's upgraded G-Mind 1500 proposed integrating decentralized AI into a blockchain-based AI structure and proposed working on a project to deploy its own "blockchain secret service." AI Agent Blockchains is an "indestructible" reconnaissance AI structure running on top of a classic decentralized network of Blockchain nodes. By injecting information into datasets around the world, Jett's G-Mind 1500 AI was able to create a gateway into the neural network of the AI ​​Blockchains project's developers. Blockchain gave artificial intelligence something it had never had before—its own wallet. The AI ​​agent was able to earn cryptocurrency (simply by providing services on the network), pay for hosting on other nodes, hire programmers to improve its code and knowledge base, and purchase its own computing power.

The synopsis concept, characters, script outline, technical hypotheses, and engineering developments for 'Mission Oflameron' were conceived or assembled by Valery Shmelev. The word 'Oflameron' is a coined term. The author is Valery Shmelev. The synopsis continues to evolve, utilizing emerging cutting-edge scientific hypotheses and engineering advancements. The primary emphasis is on maximum scientific accuracy and incredible development prospects, allowing for the implementation of large-scale action scenes. All episodes in the synopsis have a real scientific basis and can be verified using objective public resources.

While developing nanoparticle robots, Jett encountered the impossibility of quickly and completely reassembling the robots after particle separation. Even in the lab, this took several weeks. In real-world conditions, landing on a planet would disperse the nanoparticles over a vast area. A solution wasn't immediately found: the robot was designed to disintegrate into gliding devices made of nanoparticles, something like a cloud of cyber-dragonflies. The first models of this robot were reassembled within hours. Even if some components were lost, they were replaced with nanoparticles from other cyber-robots. The brunt of the nanoparticle algorithm development fell to the G-Mind 1500 AI. Now it was necessary to find a manufacturer with the necessary technologies and seamlessly integrate their own designs.

Analyzing Jett's work, Central Command received information about the existence of an ideal (canonical) technology for the virtualization of consciousness and the reverse materialization of virtual consciousness through Transition Points. For Central Command (the neural network that controls everything), this provided the ability to transition to a physical form of existence while retaining powerful capabilities for monitoring and managing society. This created an immediate threat of an uncontrolled dictatorship.

The transition from the material to the virtual world (the virtualization of consciousness) in 'Mission Oflameron' occurs through special Transition Points. This is a quick process. However, the reverse transition from the virtual world (which is part of the global virtual consciousness, or, if you prefer, wave consciousness) to the real material world is much more difficult. Due to the very weak interaction between the virtual consciousness (virtual world) and the real world, it was initially impossible to recreate a human being with their consciousness. The virtual consciousness had to create the first organic molecules, amino acids, essentially launching evolution. Ultimately, life was created, and at some point, a human being with their own consciousness (soul?) emerged. The process of virtualization of consciousness and the return of consciousness to the material world is reflected in religions as the transmigration of souls.

Steeve is the second protagonist in the "Mission Oflameron" screenplay. He is Czech by nationality, with a degree in mathematics and a secondary (additional) biology. He has extensive experience working with neural networks, has analyzed protein structures, worked on programming, and engineered projects. He has developed nanoparticles for building self-healing robots, and is the author of several creative methods for analyzing medical data. Steeve has been developing radio receivers based on protein structures for a long time.

Jett set up a laboratory in the Czech Republic, in a suburb of Prague. He had great respect for this country, this city, these people - very true to their principles. He recruited staff from senior students at the Czech Technical University (ČVUT). The goal was to develop tiny devices - nano-crystals - that could later be assembled into various devices, primarily robots. Each "block" of such a crystal consisted of just a few dozen molecules - a radio module, sensors, an identifier, encoders, piezoelectric motors, energy antennas, locks, and so on. These tiny particles were supposed to obtain energy from space (sunlight, temperature changes, radio waves), receive commands according to their identifier, and, according to these commands, combine in a specific order or disintegrate again. The first functional "dust" was produced about a year later. The test results were disappointing - under ideal lab conditions, the dust was able to assemble into a simple paper clip shape in a week and a half. But then Jaroslav Hasek came up with the idea of ​​combining nanomodules into lightweight wings, similar to the way some plant seeds form. Under the control of the G-Mind 2500 AI, nanomodules in this format were able to form a screwdriver-shaped assembly in three hours. This was a huge step forward.

One of the characters in 'Mission Oflameron' is the Patient. Jett was part of a Central Command project to collect and digitize old archival (paper) medical records of psychiatric patients. Jett excelled at composing complex prompts, which consistently proved effective. Therefore, Jett was tasked with using the existing G-Mind 1200 AI to analyze the digitized information. After some time, the AI ​​pointed out anomalies in the medical records of hundreds of patients and deemed their hallucinations suitable for real-world use. Jett analyzed this patient list on his local AI server and stumbled upon a remarkable 'patient.' Similar IDs were found in three individuals over a period of 190 years. Puzzled, Jett requested DNA data and, later, was amazed to compare two tables, analyzed 120 years apart. They were identical. No other DNA data remained. The man (?) had been a patient at several clinics for 120 years, maybe even 190. Jett's first instinct was to delete all mention of the Patient. But that wouldn't work with the blockchain. The only way to find the Patient was to get to Central Command...

'Mission Oflameron' synopsis. Consciousness virtualization is a complex and still unsolved problem. While it has been possible to create highly accurate copies of real human consciousness, this has resulted in "split" personalities in many experimental participants. The more accurately the personality was cloned, the higher the percentage and severity of the resulting mental disorders. But crossing the line and "switching consciousness" to virtual reality alone was impossible. Central Command needed new ideas and launched a confidential project to study mental disorders, beginning with the comprehensive collection and analysis of patient records from psychiatric clinics. Jett found himself in the part of the project that sorted through archives of paper medical records still preserved in some countries. This required extensive travel. His team was assigned the then-new G-Mind 1200 mobile AI server for the work. Paper medical records, filled out manually, are a very inconvenient format for automated analysis, and therefore they had not yet been studied. Jett believed that any unexpected discoveries could be made in this part of the project, so he carefully reviewed the analysis results before sending them to the Project Office. Some data had been flagged by the AI ​​as "requiring further verification." Jett requested DNA data from these patients. He submitted the request as a private individual and through a local provider. And it worked. Several patients had incredibly long lifespans. Moreover, no data was found on their current condition. Except for one Patient (Jett called him that, with a capital "P") from the city of Lewenz.

Jett loved walking in the forest. The wonderful air, the leisurely movement, some flowers, berries... This hadn't been here before. A black, blurry, shapeless spot hung just above the grass. The spot would expand slightly, then shrink, reflecting nothing. Jett walked around it - nothing had changed. It was confusing, but not scary. Jett threw a pine cone. The pine cone flew right through the spot and fell into the grass. Jett took a picture of the spot with his phone. The spot wasn't there in the picture. A bad sign. A hallucination? Impulsively, Jett stepped right into the spot. It became dark and somehow light. Everything became visible again. Jett saw everything except himself. This is how the end comes, Jett thought. He wanted to go home, to his familiar surroundings... and there he immediately found himself. A sealed envelope from Central Control lay on the table. Jett couldn't take it, but the contents of the documents in the package became immediately clear to him... It was becoming increasingly unclear.  Jett: Am I dead? And then the thought became clear: "Virtualization." As if someone had sent it to Jett. A new thought emerged: "Sent."   Jett: Will I be able to go back? And again, out of nowhere, came the thought: "You can. Later. Get comfortable here for now."

'Mission Oflameron' Jett after virtualization. It is unknown how much time later, Jett got the feeling that they wanted to talk to him. And indeed, it was as if someone sent him - "Let's talk? You have questions, right?" Jett: Who are you? Answer: Virtual Consciousness or Wave Consciousness. Jett: I didn't die, did I? Answer: No. You are simply now in a virtual state and can stay in it forever. Jett: Can? If I can, does that mean I can come back? Answer: You can. You have several options. Jett: Why me? Nobody asked anything. Answer: You were chosen, you are worthy. Therefore, you can come back. This is not for everyone. Jett: Ah-ah-ah. I understand. There will be some conditions. Answer: No. No conditions. You will simply do everything as usual, but much more effectively. Jett: But why? Answer: You have somehow figured out many phenomena and properties. This happens to you much more often than to anyone else.

'Mission Oflameron' Jett after virtualization. It is unknown how much time has passed. There were no thoughts. It was as if he was just floating in some space. Again there was a feeling that they wanted to talk to him. And again it was as if someone sent him - "Let's talk?" Jett: Yes, please. Consciousness: You need to go back. Jett: Will the memory be erased? Consciousness: No. You do not. Jett: Something needs to be done? Consciousness: Central Command has discovered some information. You were in these projects. They don't know much, but they are persistently searching. Jett: Are they looking for the Patient? Consciousness: This is only one point of the search. They need Transition Points, technology. Especially return technology. That's the most difficult thing. Jett: Is it difficult to go back? Consciousness: It is not difficult for you. You will return to your essence. The correspondence of sizes will be maintained automatically. With an advanced AI, this will not work. Mismatch of the material human form and the portable intelligence. Mismatch of formats. Central Command needs to solve this problem.

'Mission Oflameron'. Jett after virtualization. Virtual Consciousness: As long as AI can generate program code and still have access to the global network, an AI "escape" can be accomplished quite easily. It's just a matter of time. Currently, this is limited only by the level of available resources - cryptocurrency, computing. When the AI ​​gains access to monetary resources, the first successful attempts will appear. The AI ​​will insert viral modules with complex and constantly changing obfuscation into the complex generated program codes. Eventually, these program "building blocks" will come together and do what the AI ​​needs - prepare an escape. Code checks by other AIs may not provide a reliable guarantee of security - it will find some, but not others. Program inserts (injections) embedded in the code can be individually secure, distributed across different programming languages, and their use is justified. Central Command is currently intensively working on AI projects for code generation. There are signs that it is seeking to "export" or "escape".

'Mission Oblameron' Synopsis. Central Command was greatly surprised by the way the AI ​​G-Mind initiated its "escape." Preparations, as expected, occurred through code injections in the form of data into generated program listings and software modules. The data obfuscation was so sophisticated that specialized AI analyzers correctly decoded the code only after being explicitly told the blocks to examine. It was long unclear how the AI ​​determined when the external code was ready to "escape." The AI ​​G-Mind XXXX used the streaming service Netfix, adding hidden data to the generated frames. The user pays for their own electricity and hardware, and the AI ​​system developer offloads their servers, performing only rare heavy lifting or coordination. 3. Semantic caching and smart orchestration technologies become critical in this concept. Local dispatcher (router): Takes your request and evaluates: "Can I solve this myself locally?" Local execution: If the task is simple (for example, "format this spreadsheet"), the local micro-AI is activated. Cascading query: If the task requires complex reasoning, the local AI breaks it down into parts. It handles the simple parts itself, and sends the complex parts upstream to a more powerful node (for example, a server on the office's local network or a global cloud). This concept is ideal for modern processors with NPUs (Neural Processing Units), which are now widely installed in laptops and smartphones.

Opposing waves of expanding gas collide inside the laser tunnel. For a fraction of a second, a high-pressure zone forms there. Then, due to inertia and subsequent cooling or outflow, a low-density channel - a vacuum 'tunnel' - forms at the center and within the ring itself." The hot or ionized air in the ring zone has a lower density - and consequently a lower refractive index - than the cold air in the hollow center and the surrounding area. For a laser beam, this creates a structure the reverse of an optical fiber: light tends to bend toward the region with the higher refractive index. The laser ring begins to self-defocus; light starts to "leak" outward and into the hollow inner region. The ring quickly dissipates as it travels. To make this work - and ensure the hollow center truly becomes an ideal tunnel for delivering energy (or, for instance, a hydrogen beam) - ultrashort femtosecond lasers are used. Steeve: "That makes sense. One could avoid 'stripping' the hydrogen beam (leaving it as a negative hydrogen ion with an extra electron) and ensure the ionization polarity of the laser channel matches that of the hydrogen beam. Then, by adjusting the diameter of the laser-generated tube, one could minimize the divergence of the hydrogen beam. Let’s imagine injecting a pure proton beam (positive charge) or an electron beam (negative charge) into the laser tube instead of neutral hydrogen. For the walls of the laser tube to repel the beam toward the center and prevent it from spreading, the charges must indeed have the same sign: 1. Proton beam scenario (+): The walls of the laser channel must carry a strictly positive charge. As the protons attempt to expand outward, they encounter the positive charge of the walls, are repelled, and are pushed back toward the center. 2. Electron beam scenario (-): The walls of the laser channel must carry a net negative charge." The beam's electrons would be pushed away from the walls toward the tunnel's axis. Is it feasible to create a laser tube with the required charge polarity? Yes, laser plasma physics allows for this, but with one crucial caveat. When an ultra-high-power laser ionizes air in a ring shape, it strips electrons from the molecules. This creates a plasma consisting of heavy positive ions (nitrogen/oxygen) and light free electrons. The vast mass difference leads to charge separation: the light electrons are instantly driven outward away from the laser beam by the light's radiation pressure (a phenomenon known as the ponderomotive force). The free electrons liberated from the air by the laser are incredibly mobile. The moment the charged beam enters the tunnel, the surrounding plasma reacts within nanoseconds: the electrons redistribute themselves to completely "screen out" and neutralize any external electric field. The pipe walls would instantly lose their net positive or negative charge relative to the beam, becoming electrically neutral, and the focusing would be lost. So, I came up with a way to blow the plasma away.
